refutation_attempt: Read EasyGL's Clear and every sibling clear entry, the D3D9 clear gates and their bind sites, and the pinning tests. Both named defects are fixed, but comparing the sibling clears found one that skips the write-mask restore the others perform, which OpenGL4's twin route documents.
reason: Both named defects are fixed: EasyGL's colour clear touches colour only and D3D9 gates on the bound target's depth format. A narrower EasyGL clear defect survives: ClearColorAndStencil forces the stencil write mask open and never restores it, unlike the other mask-overriding clears; OpenGL4's twin route says so in a comment, and only the stencil-only route is tested.

entry.title: EasyGL family: ClearColorAndStencil leaves the stencil write mask forced to all ones, so a later draw ignores StencilWriteMask
entry.summary: GraphicsDevice::Clear with Target and Stencil reaches EasyGLRenderer::ClearColorAndStencil, which forces the GL stencil mask open and never restores it, unlike the other EasyGL clears (REMED-GFX-237). A later StencilWriteMask-limited draw is not limited.
entry.expected: XNA's Clear ignores StencilWriteMask but does not change the device's DepthStencilState, so a draw after the clear obeys the state the game assigned. EasyGL's own rule (REMED-GFX-237, stated in EasyGLRenderer.hpp and in OpenGL4Renderer.cpp) is that every clear puts back the write masks it forced open, because a game need not reassign its DepthStencilState before the next draw.
entry.actual: EasyGLRenderer::ClearColorAndDepth, ClearDepth, ClearStencil, ClearDepthAndStencil and ClearColorDepthAndStencil all call RestoreWriteMasksAfterClear. ClearColorAndStencil sets the stencil mask to all ones, clears, and restores only the colour mask and the scissor. After GraphicsDevice::Clear(ClearOptions::Target | ClearOptions::Stencil, ...) the GL stencil write mask stays 0xFFFFFFFF until ApplyDepthStencilState runs again, so a draw through a state with StencilWriteMask 0 or a partial mask writes stencil bits the state forbids. OpenGL4Renderer::ClearColorAndStencil carries a comment that EasyGL's twin of this route does not put the mask back. The restore check in easygl_graphicsdevice_clear_stencil_test.cpp (Check D) uses ClearOptions::Stencil only.

sources.note: ClearColorAndStencil has no RestoreWriteMasksAfterClear; ClearStencil and ClearColorDepthAndStencil do

SDL_GPU's generator expands the Vulkan renderer's shadow_sampling.glsl, so one edit reaches two headers; the commit that added that coupling recorded a hand check that Vulkan's header still regenerates byte for byte.
